newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan CPC cracker hit power blip to reopen Monday.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan CPC cracker hit power blip to reopen Monday.

text.p: Taiwan state oil monopoly Chinese Petroleum Corp said it would reopen on Monday its No.5 naphtha cracker in Kaohsiung, which was shut down in a brief but costly power failure on Thursday.
"It will take four days to prepare the cracker for reopening, so we expect production to resume on Monday," a Chinese Petroleum official said on Friday.
The official estimated the losses due to the power failure and shutdown at T$100 million.
Local media have estimated the total cost to Chinese Petroleum and several other affected firms

The two-minute outage on Thursday was likely to cause a total of T$400 million (U$14 million) or more in losses to Chinese Petroleum and other major firms operating in or near Kaohsiung's Jenta petrochemical park, Taiwan media estimated.
Chinese Petroleum shut down its No.5 naphtha cracker, which has annual production capacity of 400,000 tonnes of ethylene, and as well as a score of affiliated petrochemical facilities.
Officials at electrical utility Taiwan Power Co, which supplies the Jenta park, said they were at a loss to explain why power failed.

Other petrochemical firms affected were Formosa Plastics Group members Formosa Plastics Corp and Nan Ya Plastics Corp as well as China Petrochem Corp, Grand Petrochem Corp, USI Far East Corp and China Manmade Corp, the park said.
